extracted.intended_audience: new peer reviewers of biomedical/scientific research papers (early-career researchers, invited reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing a peer review of a scientific (biomedical) manuscript: what to read, what to evaluate (structure, methods, results, ethics, citations), and how to present feedback and a recommendation. Intended as a stepwise checklist for new reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Why have you been asked, what should you focus on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the role requested by the editor (e.g., full review, methodological check, specialty opinion) and the scope/priorities for your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize yourself with the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Read thoroughly; grasp question, methodology, analysis, results, conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do an initial complete read to understand the central question and the paper's approach before forming detailed critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate structure and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess organization, abstract quality, intro effectiveness, logical flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether sections are well organized, the abstract accurately summarizes the work, the introduction motivates the study, and the manuscript flows logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess appropriateness and rigor of design and statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if the study design, experimental procedures, controls, sample sizes, and statistical methods are suitable to answer the research question and are performed rigorously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate results and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Does data support the question? Are statistics appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the presented data actually address the hypotheses, whether analyses are correctly applied and interpreted, and whether figures/tables clearly present results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess discussion and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Balanced analysis; conclusions aligned with objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the authors' interpretation is balanced, acknowledges limitations, and whether conclusions follow logically from the results without overreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines, informed consent, confidentiality, harm minimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify compliance with ethical standards (ethics committee approvals, informed consent for human subjects, animal welfare statements), data privacy/confidentiality measures, and any potential harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify references and citations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citations support claims, key literature is cited, references are current, and there are no obvious miscitations or missing important prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer actionable, specific suggestions for improvement, note strengths as well as weaknesses, and maintain a respectful, professional tone focused on the manuscript, not the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize your review
rubrics_metrics.description: Main points, strengths, weaknesses, overall recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude with a concise summary highlighting the most important issues, the manuscript’s main strengths and weaknesses, and a clear recommendation to the editor (e.g., accept, revise, reject).
